presentation.label: STASIS
presentation.summary: A footswitch freeze: turn it on and the note you just played holds while you play over it.
presentation.overview: Stasis keeps listening while it is off. Turn it on with the footswitch and it holds the last moments you played as a seamless loop, while your dry signal stays open on top; turn it off to let go. Length, Blur, Decay and Tone shape the hold, and Capture can hold or release independently of the footswitch.
highlights: Holds what you just played, captured looking back
Seamless loop with a crossfade that scales with its length
Decay from a slow fade to an endless hold
usage: Put Stasis in a patch, leave Capture at 0 and play a note.
Turn Stasis on with the footswitch: what you just played holds while you play over it.
Turn it off to let go. Length, Blur, Decay and Tone shape the hold.

access.location: The pedal's effect list, Delay group, as Stasis.
steps: Add Stasis to a patch from the effect list (Delay group).
Its knobs are on the effect's pages, three per page.

controls.name: Length
controls.doc: Loop length, about 60 ms to 1.4 s, live.

controls.name: Blur
controls.doc: Crossfade at the loop seam, as a share of the loop.

controls.name: Decay
controls.doc: How the hold fades; fully up holds for ever.

controls.name: Tone
controls.doc: Low-pass on the held layer only; the dry stays open.

controls.name: Mix
controls.doc: Dry and wet blend while it holds; idle passes dry at unity.

controls.name: Capture
controls.doc: 0 = the footswitch captures and releases; 1 = release; 2 = capture and hold regardless of the footswitch.

limitations: A patch loads with nothing held: it never freezes on load.
Built with the init path off: a recalled patch plays the knobs' defaults until you touch a knob.

load.conditions: The cost Stasis declares in its descriptor, which the pedal adds up per patch; not read from the DSP meter.

hardware.summary: The release file was on the pedal (read back over USB with the same SHA-256): the pedal booted, the effect showed its screen and did its job.
limitations: One run, reported by the tester as working; nothing measured.
Built with the init path off: the sound takes saved knob values only once a knob is touched.
MIDISTOMP V2.0.1 on Zoom's 2.10, not Zoom's 2.10 alone.

tests.summary: The release file has no code from Zoom's effects (check_no_stock.py), passes Ziddle's loader check, renders in Ziddle, and ran on an MS-70CDR.
